messages:
viv: FYI - us-east-1 GPU fleet observed a wave of failed keystore decrypts after the SNI inspection rule change rolled out. A bunch of warm-pool nodes stayed in ProvisioningPending.
oliver: Which rule? We only changed the TLS inspection policy to enforce SNI allowlists for outbound 443.
viv: The allowlist omitted kms.redwood.internal and the private KMS endpoint hostnames. The inspection device returned TCP reset when the SNI didn't match, so the keystore-proxy tls handshake failed.
sylvia: That matches the node logs I pulled. Paste: ```
keystore-proxy ERR: tls handshake error: remote reset (sni not allowed) host=kms.redwood.internal:443
agent: join state=ProvisioningPending reason="keystore decrypt timeout" attempts=5
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: sni-policy v1.4.0 applied to us-east-1 edge-inspectors at 2026-03-25T02:10Z.
oliver: Urg, role boundary prevents me from editing the SNI policy directly. Need net-security to whitelist the KMS names.
viv: Temp mitigation: created an exception record and opened a direct NAT path for the keystore-proxy instances to bypass the inspector using `infractl egress-bypass create --tag warm-pool-useast --dest-host kms.redwood.internal --port 443 --ttl 20m`. Nodes recovered in ~7m.
ops-bot: monitor: warm-pool-useast healthy_nodes: 11 -> 57 (7m).
sylvia: Cost impact: churn + double-warmups triggered an autoscaler correction and consumed ~5.4 GPU-hours. Preliminary cost delta ~USD 1.5k.
oliver: Immediate follow-ups: (1) add KMS hostname to SNI allowlist and re-run a canary; (2) add a pre-deploy check that queries the SNI policy for required service hostnames; (3) create a scoped operator role so SRE can create short-lived bypasses without full net-admin perms, with mandatory audit log.
viv: Also propose: treat private KMS endpoints as a special case - always allow SNI to those hostnames during rollout windows and block after canary success. That prevents silent breakages.
compliance-bot: exception logged id=EXC-US-2026-901; operator=viv; reason="keystore egress bypass while SNI allowlist updated"; expires=2026-03-25T02:30Z. Audit record attached.
sylvia: I'll open RED-SEC-7789 for the policy gating and RED-OPS-3301 for the operator role. Attaching logs and cost estimate.
viv: For rollout hygiene: recommend ordering change where allowlist additions are applied before deny/enforce rules, plus an automated probe that performs a KMS decrypt from a canary warm-pool instance as part of policy rollout.
oliver: Agreed. Also note we should avoid blanket SNI denies for service hostnames that are resolved via internal DNS -> private endpoints.
viv: Filed incident: https://issues.internal/RED-IF-7789 "SNI inspection rollout omitted KMS hostnames -> keystore decrypt failures -> GPU warm-pool churn". Linking exception id and cost snapshot.
ops-bot: tagging on-call team and scheduling a follow-up postmortem meeting.
